answer.evidence: The image is a full 96x96 tile seen from directly above. Dirt covers the whole tile, and a mottled grey asphalt L shape (rows 18-78) sits on it. Both are flat textured surfaces with no foreshortened top band, no ellipse and no roof plane. The only vertical-looking element is a 1-3 row dark brown ledge at rows 76-78 under the asphalt. That is below the 3-row minimum for a front face, so it is a thin edge shadow and not a south face. The drawing reads as a flat ground decal, consistent with the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and just under the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no flat fills. The dirt carries speckle and grain in several browns. The asphalt has dotted crumbs and a lighter broken edge, with a darker ledge on the south side. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the edges lean brown or grey-brown rather than black, which reads as dark_material_tone with no sticker outline. Each material has about 4 steps against 5-6 in the references, and only 9 distinct colours in total, so it is slightly shallower. That is about what a locked palette allows for a small corner patch, and it is not flatter than the grass reference. A careful artist would accept it beside the references.
